core.title: Register each feature in exactly one product capability manifest
core.given: A feature exists in the plan, and product capability manifests (each product capability's list of the features it owns) record which product capability owns which feature.
core.when: You create, change (including edits that touch only a feature's acceptance or plan-artifact content), move, remove or assess any feature, or edit a product capability manifest. A feature already listed in exactly one manifest is compliant and needs no registration change.
core.then: Register each feature under exactly one product capability's manifest.
prefer: Add the feature's entry to its owning product capability's manifest in the same change that creates the feature, following the entry format already used in that manifest.
When moving a feature between product capabilities, remove the entry from the old product capability's manifest and add it to the new one in the same change.
Where the repository's layout places features under their owning product capability's tree, list the feature in that product capability's manifest so that manifest ownership and location agree.
avoid: Orphan features that no product capability manifest lists.
Listing the same feature in two or more product capabilities' manifests.
Leaving stale manifest entries that point to removed or renamed features.
core.why: A feature belongs to exactly one product capability; the product capability manifest is the link that makes that ownership explicit and traceable.
evidence: Every feature id appears in exactly one product capability's manifest; none appear in zero or several.
Proposed verification approach (not a source requirement): a reviewer checks the change to confirm that new or moved features have matching manifest entries added and old ones removed.
verification: Disposition documentation-only, severity 2: the obligation is documented and this rule requires no automated detector; the source does not say how compliance is established.
The source defines no manifest entry schema and no path-to-capability mapping; compliance uses the entry format already present in the repository's manifests.

A check, if realized, needs a repository-wide observer that extracts every feature id and cross-references all capability-manifest entries, so pre-existing orphans and duplicates surface even without a lifecycle change; such a check covers only the exactly-one registration, not manifest entry format or feature location.

Proposed, not a source requirement: a reviewer examines the change to confirm that new or moved features have matching manifest entries added and old ones removed. Review is one possible approach, not a required one.

fires: Planner adds a new feature but does not list it in any product capability's manifest.
Planner moves a feature to another product capability and lists it in both the old and new product capability manifests.
Planner edits a product capability's manifest to add or remove a feature entry.
Planner reviews or plans work on an existing feature and discovers it is listed in no product capability manifest, or in more than one, even though nothing about it is being changed.

Planner edits only the acceptance or plan-artifact content of a feature: the rule applies; if the feature is already listed in exactly one product capability manifest it is compliant and no registration change is needed, otherwise the registration must be repaired.
doesNotFire: Changes that touch neither features nor product capability manifests and whose task does not concern features, product capabilities or manifests (e.g. pure implementation code with no plan artifacts).

profileRequirements.meaning: The name pattern(s) that identify plan-artifact files; here the pattern that identifies the product capability manifest, so every reference to 'a product capability's manifest' and the manifest task term resolve to a concrete file.

How a plan artifact is assigned its kind, distinguishing the capability-manifest kind from other plan-artifact kinds such as features; in the Bun realization the manifest is identified by file name, wherever it lives in the repository.
profileRequirements.bunValue: capability_manifest = the product capability's _features.yaml that lists its features.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds this rule scopes to and references: the feature kind, the capability-manifest kind, and the concrete plan-item kind whose content an acceptance-only edit may touch.
profileRequirements.bunValue: feature, capability_manifest (activation file kinds); DESIRED OUTCOME (plan-item kind named in the when clause)

bunOnly.text: path_glob: **/_features.yaml (product capability manifests are identifiable by file name; no particular plan directory layout is assumed)
bunOnly.reason: The neutral activation fact vocabulary has no path_glob fact type; the core scopes by file_kind, and the manifest's identifying name pattern is carried by suffix.plan_artifact.

bunOnly.text: Parity records implementation_preserved=false (no detector implementation was carried over).
bunOnly.reason: Parity and extraction bookkeeping of the ATDD-Bun rewrite; the core keeps only the generic verification facts (disposition, severity, unspecified compliance method, no manifest entry schema or path-to-capability mapping).

neutralityNotes: 'Feature' and 'product capability' are ATDD planning concepts and stay in the core. The capability-manifest file is identified with existing vocabulary only: suffix.plan_artifact carries the name pattern (**/_features.yaml) and roles.assignment distinguishes the capability-manifest kind among plan artifacts; no new identification key is proposed. The path_glob activation fact type has no neutral counterpart and stays bunOnly, with the core scoping by file_kind. 'DESIRED OUTCOME' is neutralized to 'plan-artifact content' in the core and realized as a concrete plan-artifact kind through roles.plan_artifact.kinds. prefer[2]'s conditional ownership/location preference remains core text because the Bun text supplies no directory pattern (no path-to-capability mapping), so layout.feature_dir is not claimed as a profile value. Compliance method stays unspecified: disposition documentation-only and severity 2 are per-rule verification facts, and reviewer review appears only as an explicitly proposed approach, never as a required check.
